chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Isa ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, via a chain belonging to him, said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him: 'The boundary of the Mosque of Kufa is the end of the Sarrajin [lineage/descendants of Adam] (peace be upon him), and I dislike entering it while mounted.'

I said: 'Then who changed it from its line?' He said: 'As for the first of that, it was the Flood in the time of Noah (peace be upon him). Then the companions of Kisra and al-Nu'man changed it. Then Ziyad ibn Abi Sufyan changed it, curse of Allah be upon him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the historical boundary of the Mosque of Kufa according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) delineates the historical evolution of the Mosque of Kufa’s boundaries, tracing its original extent to the lineage of Adam and noting his preference for entering on foot as a sign of humility. He attributes subsequent alterations to three major historical events: the Flood of Noah, the administrative changes under the Kisra dynasty, and the specific modifications by Ziyad ibn Abi Sufyan, whose curse is invoked, highlighting the political and spiritual significance of this sacred space in Shia tradition.
